innodb_adaptive_flushing.desc: This parameter specifies whether to dynamically adjust the flush rate of dirty pages in the InnoDB buffer pool based on workload. Enabling adaptive flushing can improve performance and alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks. When set to ON, adaptive flushing is enabled; when set to OFF, it is disabled

innodb_adaptive_flushing_lwm.desc: Defines the low watermark for adaptive flushing as a percentage of redo log capacity. Increasing this value can improve write performance but may increase recovery time, helping to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks. Default value is 10

innodb_adaptive_hash_index.desc: Adaptive Hash Index is a mechanism that allows InnoDB to dynamically create hash indexes based on query patterns to accelerate queries. It can alleviate CPU bottlenecks and improve query performance. When set to ON, it is enabled; when set to OFF, it is disabled

innodb_adaptive_hash_index_parts.desc: Number of partitions for InnoDB Adaptive Hash Index. Increasing this value can improve hash index performance but may increase memory usage. Can alleviate memory bottlenecks. Default value is 8, maximum is 512, minimum is 1

innodb_adaptive_max_sleep_delay.desc: This parameter allows InnoDB to automatically adjust the value of innodb_thread_sleep_delay based on current workload. It defines the maximum delay time (in microseconds) during adaptive maximum sleep delay, which can help alleviate CPU bottlenecks, especially in high concurrency scenarios. Increasing this value allows InnoDB to sleep longer when waiting for locks, thereby reducing CPU usage; decreasing this value makes InnoDB attempt to acquire locks faster

innodb_api_bk_commit_interval.desc: This parameter defines the auto-commit time interval (in seconds) for idle connections in the InnoDB memcached interface. Increasing this value reduces the frequency of commit operations, thereby helping to alleviate CPU bottlenecks; decreasing this value increases the frequency of commit operations, which may affect performance

innodb_api_disable_rowlock.desc: This parameter is used to disable row locking for InnoDB API during DML operations. When set to ON, row locking is disabled; when set to OFF, row locking is enabled. Disabling row locking may lead to performance degradation, but in some cases can help alleviate CPU bottlenecks

innodb_buffer_pool_chunk_size.desc: This parameter defines the size of each chunk in the InnoDB buffer pool (in bytes). Increasing this value reduces the number of chunks, thereby reducing management overhead; decreasing this value increases the number of chunks, which may improve concurrency performance. This parameter is very important for alleviating memory bottlenecks

innodb_buffer_pool_dump_at_shutdown.desc: Indicates whether to dump the contents of the buffer pool at shutdown. Enabling this option can improve performance at next startup. When set to ON, it is enabled; when set to OFF, it is disabled

innodb_buffer_pool_dump_now.desc: This parameter is used to immediately dump the contents of the InnoDB buffer pool to disk. It is typically used in conjunction with the parameter innodb_buffer_pool_load_now, helping to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks, especially when quick data recovery is needed after restart. When set to ON, it means immediate dump; when set to OFF, it means no dump

innodb_buffer_pool_dump_pct.desc: This parameter defines the percentage of pages to dump during buffer pool dump. It specifies the percentage of recently used pages in each buffer pool for faster data recovery at restart. Increasing this value can speed up data recovery at restart, while decreasing this value reduces the amount of dumped data, thereby helping to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks

innodb_buffer_pool_instances.desc: Sets the number of buffer pool instances, allowing multiple buffer pool instances to process requests in parallel to improve performance. Can alleviate memory bottlenecks. Recommended to use multiple instances when buffer pool size is greater than 1GB

innodb_buffer_pool_in_core_file.desc: This parameter indicates whether to write the contents of the InnoDB buffer pool to core dump files. Disabling this parameter can reduce core file size, suitable for troubleshooting. When set to ON, it is enabled; when set to OFF, it is disabled

innodb_buffer_pool_load_at_startup.desc: Indicates whether the InnoDB buffer pool automatically loads previously held pages at MySQL server startup to improve startup performance. When set to ON, it is enabled; when set to OFF, it is disabled

innodb_buffer_pool_load_now.desc: This parameter is used to immediately load the contents of the InnoDB buffer pool, helping to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks, especially when quick data recovery is needed after restart. When set to ON, it means immediate load; when set to OFF, it means no load

innodb_buffer_pool_size.desc: Sets the size of the InnoDB buffer pool, which is used to cache data and indexes to improve performance. Increasing this value reduces disk I/O and improves read performance. Recommended to set to 70%-80% of system memory. This is one of the most important parameters for InnoDB, directly affecting database performance and response speed

innodb_change_buffering.desc: This parameter controls how InnoDB buffers changes to secondary indexes, optimizing write operations and alleviating disk I/O bottlenecks. Optional values include: none (disabled), inserts (inserts only), deletes (deletes only), changes (changes), purges (purges), and all (all)

innodb_change_buffer_max_size.desc: This parameter defines the maximum size of the InnoDB change buffer (expressed as a percentage), as a percentage of the total buffer pool size. Increasing this value can improve write performance and help alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks, while decreasing this value limits the size of the change buffer and may affect performance

innodb_checksum_algorithm.desc: Specifies how to generate and verify checksums for disk blocks stored in InnoDB tablespaces to ensure data integrity. Can alleviate CPU bottlenecks. Optional values include crc32, strict_crc32, innodb, strict_innodb, none, and strict_none. Recommended to use crc32 for better performance and security

innodb_commit_concurrency.desc: This parameter controls the number of transactions that can commit simultaneously, allowing multiple threads to commit concurrently to improve performance. Proper adjustment of this parameter can alleviate CPU bottlenecks. Recommended to adjust based on system load, typically set to 8 or 16

innodb_compression_level.desc: Specifies the zlib compression level for InnoDB compressed tables and indexes. This parameter controls the strength of data compression and can alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks. Value range is from 0 (no compression) to 9 (maximum compression). Increasing this value increases CPU usage but reduces disk space usage

innodb_compression_pad_pct_max.desc: This parameter defines the maximum percentage of padding for InnoDB compressed pages. It specifies the maximum percentage of free space that can be reserved in each compressed page. Increasing this value can improve compression efficiency, while decreasing this value may lead to reduced compression efficiency, thereby helping to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks

innodb_concurrency_tickets.desc: This parameter defines the number of concurrency tickets for InnoDB, determining how many threads can enter InnoDB simultaneously. Increasing this value can improve concurrency performance and help alleviate CPU bottlenecks, while decreasing this value may lead to performance degradation

innodb_ddl_threads.desc: This parameter defines the maximum number of parallel threads that can be used by InnoDB when executing DDL operations. Increasing this value can improve the concurrency of DDL operations and help alleviate CPU bottlenecks, while decreasing this value may lead to performance degradation

innodb_disable_sort_file_cache.desc: This parameter is used to disable the operating system file system cache for temporary files during merge sorts to improve performance. Enabling this parameter (value ON) can help alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks, while disabling the cache (value OFF) may lead to performance degradation

innodb_doublewrite.desc: Controls the doublewrite buffer mechanism to improve data security. Can alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks. MySQL 8.0.30 and later versions support multiple settings. When set to ON, it is enabled; when set to OFF, it is disabled. DETECT_AND_RECOVER and DETECT_ONLY are used for detection and recovery. Recommended to keep enabled to prevent data loss

innodb_fast_shutdown.desc: Controls InnoDB's fast shutdown behavior, affecting performance and data security during shutdown. Can alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks. Values are 0 (full shutdown), 1 (fast shutdown), 2 (minimal shutdown). Recommended to use 1 to balance performance and security

innodb_file_per_table.desc: Enables the use of separate tablespace files for each table to improve management flexibility and performance, alleviating disk I/O bottlenecks. When set to ON, it is enabled; when set to OFF, it is disabled

innodb_flushing_avg_loops.desc: This parameter defines the number of flush iterations InnoDB maintains in the running average. It controls how many iterations InnoDB keeps a snapshot of the previously calculated flush state, thus affecting how quickly adaptive flushing responds to changing workloads. Increasing this value reduces the frequency of flush operations, potentially helping to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks, while decreasing this value increases the frequency of flush operations, which may affect performance

innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit.desc: Controls the log flushing policy at transaction commit, affecting data security and performance. Values are 0 (flush once per second), 1 (flush at each commit), 2 (write to memory at each commit). Recommended to choose based on data security requirements. Proper adjustment can alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks

innodb_flush_method.desc: Defines the method used to flush data to InnoDB data files and log files, which affects I/O throughput. Can alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks. Optional values include fsync, O_DSYNC, littlesync, nosync, O_DIRECT, O_DIRECT_NO_FSYNC, unbuffered, and normal. Recommended to choose the appropriate flush method based on storage device

innodb_force_recovery.desc: This parameter is used to set InnoDB's forced recovery mode, typically changed during serious troubleshooting situations. It can help recover data after crashes, mainly affecting disk I/O bottlenecks. Value range is from 0 to 6, where 0 represents normal mode, and 1 to 6 represent different levels of recovery mode, with higher values having more restrictions on recovery

innodb_ft_max_token_size.desc: This parameter defines the maximum token size in InnoDB full-text indexes. It determines the maximum character length of words that can be indexed. Increasing this value allows longer words to be indexed, potentially helping to alleviate CPU bottlenecks, while decreasing this value limits the word length that can be indexed

innodb_idle_flush_pct.desc: This parameter limits the percentage of page flushing during InnoDB idle periods. Increasing this value can improve flushing frequency during idle times, thereby helping to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks; decreasing this value reduces flushing frequency during idle times, which may affect performance

innodb_io_capacity.desc: The innodb_io_capacity variable defines the number of I/O operations per second (IOPS) available to InnoDB background tasks. This parameter affects the rate at which dirty pages are flushed from the buffer. Recommended to adjust based on storage device performance, typically set to SAS 200, SSD 5000, PCI-E 10000-50000

innodb_io_capacity_max.desc: The innodb_io_capacity_max variable defines the maximum number of I/O operations per second (IOPS) for InnoDB background tasks. This parameter sets the maximum I/O capacity for InnoDB, affecting I/O rates under high load conditions, and can alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks. Recommended to adjust based on storage device performance, typically set to 1000-20000

innodb_lock_wait_timeout.desc: Time in seconds that an InnoDB transaction waits for a row lock before giving up. Default value is 50 seconds. This parameter affects transaction lock waiting behavior and can alleviate CPU bottlenecks. Recommended to adjust based on application requirements

innodb_log_buffer_size.desc: Size of InnoDB log buffer in bytes. Increasing this value can improve write performance, especially under high transaction loads, and can alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks. Default value is 16MB, minimum is 1KB, maximum is 4GB

innodb_log_files_in_group.desc: Number of log files in the InnoDB log file group. Increasing this value can improve concurrent write performance and alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks. Default value is 2, minimum is 2, maximum is 100

innodb_log_file_size.desc: Size of each InnoDB log file. Increasing this value can improve recovery performance, especially for large transactions. Can alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks. Default value is 48MB, maximum is 512GB, minimum is 1MB

innodb_max_dirty_pages_pct.desc: Maximum percentage of dirty pages allowed in InnoDB. This parameter controls the proportion of dirty pages allowed in the InnoDB buffer pool, default value is 90%. Increasing this value reduces write operations but may increase recovery time. Recommended to appropriately decrease this value when excessive memory allocation causes serious Swap usage to release Swap space. Too high a value causes too many data pages to be swapped for each update, while too low a value may slow down update operations

innodb_max_dirty_pages_pct_lwm.desc: This parameter defines the minimum percentage of dirty pages allowed in InnoDB, representing the low watermark when enabling pre-flushing to control dirty page ratio. Increasing this value reduces the frequency of write operations, while decreasing this value increases the frequency of write operations, which may affect performance

innodb_max_purge_lag.desc: Defines the desired maximum purge lag. If this value is exceeded, delays will be imposed on INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations. Increasing this value reduces the frequency of purge operations but may increase memory usage, thereby alleviating memory bottlenecks. Default value is 0, maximum is 4294967295, minimum is 0

innodb_old_blocks_pct.desc: Specifies the approximate percentage of the InnoDB buffer pool used for the old block sublist. Increasing this value can increase the use of old blocks, potentially improving query performance and alleviating memory bottlenecks. Default value is 37, maximum is 95, minimum is 5

innodb_old_blocks_time.desc: Specifies the time in milliseconds that a block must remain in the old sublist after being inserted, before it can be moved to the new sublist. Increasing this value can increase the retention time of old blocks, potentially improving query performance and alleviating memory bottlenecks. Default value is 1000 milliseconds

innodb_open_files.desc: Specifies the maximum number of files InnoDB can open simultaneously. Increasing this value can improve concurrent performance, especially under high load conditions, and can alleviate memory bottlenecks. Default value is 300

innodb_page_size.desc: Specifies the page size for InnoDB tablespaces, affecting storage efficiency and performance. Can alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks. Optional values are 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768, and 65536 bytes

innodb_parallel_read_threads.desc: Defines the number of threads that can be used for parallel clustered index reads. Increasing this value can improve read performance, especially on multi-core systems, and can alleviate CPU bottlenecks. Default value is 4, minimum is 1, maximum is 256

innodb_read_ahead_threshold.desc: Controls the sensitivity of linear read-ahead used by InnoDB to prefetch pages into the buffer pool. Increasing this value can improve sequential read performance but may increase random read latency, thereby alleviating disk I/O bottlenecks. Default value is 56, maximum is 64, minimum is 0

innodb_read_io_threads.desc: Number of I/O threads for InnoDB read operations. Increasing this value can improve read performance, especially in high concurrency scenarios, and can alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks. Default value is 4, maximum is 64, minimum is 1

innodb_sync_array_size.desc: Defines the size of the mutex/lock wait array. Increasing this value can improve thread coordination capability under high concurrent workloads, especially when there are many waiting threads. This setting must be configured at MySQL instance startup and cannot be changed afterward. Increasing this value can improve write performance, especially under high load conditions, and can alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks

innodb_table_locks.desc: If `autocommit = 0`, `InnoDB` respects `LOCK TABLES`; MySQL does not return from `LOCK TABLES ... WRITE` until all other threads have released all their locks on the table. Enables or disables InnoDB table locks. When enabled, it can improve concurrent performance and alleviate CPU bottlenecks. Values are ON/OFF, default is ON

innodb_thread_concurrency.desc: This parameter defines the maximum number of threads allowed to enter InnoDB. A value of 0 (default) means unlimited concurrency (no upper limit). In high concurrency systems, this variable is used for performance tuning. Recommended to set to 2 times the number of server CPU cores to optimize concurrent operations. Appropriate settings can improve CPU multi-core processing capability and concurrency, but values that are too high may increase context switching, thereby affecting performance

innodb_thread_sleep_delay.desc: InnoDB thread sleep delay, representing the sleep time of InnoDB threads before joining the InnoDB queue, in microseconds. Increasing this value can reduce CPU usage but may affect response time, suitable for alleviating CPU bottlenecks. Default value is 10000 microseconds, maximum is 4294967295 microseconds, minimum is 0 microseconds

innodb_write_io_threads.desc: Number of I/O threads for InnoDB write operations. Increasing this value can improve write performance, especially in high concurrency scenarios, and can alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks. Default value is 4, maximum is 64, minimum is 1

max_heap_table_size.desc: This variable sets the maximum size to which user-created MEMORY tables are permitted to grow. It can reduce disk I/O by keeping temporary tables in memory

thread_cache_size.desc: The number of threads cached to handle new connections. This variable can be increased to improve performance if you have a lot of new connections. It reduces CPU overhead from thread creation/destruction. Ideally set high enough so that most new connections use cached threads, but higher values consume more memory

tmp_table_size.desc: Defines the maximum size of internal in-memory temporary tables created by the MEMORY storage engine and, as of MySQL 8.0.28, the TempTable storage engine. If the size of a temporary table exceeds this value, it is converted to a disk-based table, which can alleviate memory and disk I/O. Higher values reduce disk usage but increase memory consumption

table_open_cache.desc: The number of open table instances for all threads. Increasing this value reduces the overhead of opening tables and improves concurrent execution efficiency, but increases memory usage. This parameter is primarily used to mitigate CPU bottlenecks, especially in high-concurrency connection scenarios

table_open_cache_instances.desc: The number of table cache instances. Partitioning the table cache into multiple independent instances reduces contention during concurrent access. Increasing this value improves scalability in high-concurrency environments, helping to mitigate CPU bottlenecks. It is recommended to increase this value when the number of connections is high

sync_binlog.desc: Controls whether the binary log is synchronized to disk after each transaction commit. When set to 1, synchronization occurs after every commit, providing the highest data safety but increasing disk I/O overhead. When set to 0, the operating system decides when to flush, which can alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks but may risk data loss

key_buffer_size.desc: The size of the buffer used for MyISAM index caches (in MB). Increasing this value improves index read performance for MyISAM tables and reduces disk I/O operations. It primarily affects disk I/O bottlenecks and should be increased appropriately for environments using the MyISAM engine

binlog_cache_size.desc: The size of the memory buffer used to cache binary log entries during a transaction (in bytes). Increasing this value reduces the number of disk writes during transaction commit, helping to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks. If large transactions are frequent, increasing this value is recommended to avoid using on-disk temporary files

innodb_purge_threads.desc: The number of background purge threads used by InnoDB to clean up undo logs and deleted rows. Increasing this value improves the parallelism of purge operations, helping to alleviate CPU bottlenecks, and can improve system responsiveness under high write loads

innodb_page_cleaners.desc: The number of page cleaner threads responsible for flushing dirty pages to disk. Increasing this value improves the parallelism of dirty page flushing, helping to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks, especially in environments with high write loads and large buffer pools

slave_parallel_type.desc: Specifies the type of parallel replication used on the replica. DATABASE mode uses database-based parallel replication, while LOGICAL_CLOCK mode uses logical clock-based parallel replication, which typically provides higher parallelism, helps alleviate CPU bottlenecks, and improves replication throughput

slave_parallel_workers.desc: The number of worker threads used for parallel replication on the replica. Increasing this value improves the parallelism of replication apply, accelerating data synchronization on the replica and helping to alleviate CPU bottlenecks. It is recommended to set this value based on CPU core count, typically between 4 and 16

slave_preserve_commit_order.desc: Controls whether the commit order of transactions is preserved on the replica. When enabled (ON), it ensures that the commit order of parallel replication transactions matches that of the source, improving data consistency but potentially increasing lock waits. This parameter is used to balance data consistency and CPU usage

lock_wait_timeout.desc: The timeout period for acquiring metadata locks (in seconds). When a session waits for a lock longer than this value, the system returns a timeout error. Increasing this value prevents long-waiting transactions from being prematurely terminated, helping to alleviate CPU bottlenecks, but may increase lock wait times

long_query_time.desc: The threshold time for the slow query log (in seconds). Queries with execution time exceeding this value are logged to the slow query log. Increasing this value reduces the amount of slow query logging, while decreasing it helps identify more performance issues. Primarily used to analyze disk I/O and CPU bottlenecks

max_allowed_packet.desc: The maximum size of a packet for communication between the client and server (in bytes). Increasing this value supports larger data transfers (e.g., BLOB fields) but increases memory usage. Primarily used to mitigate network transmission bottlenecks; the default of 67108864 (64MB) is suitable for most scenarios

max_connections.desc: The maximum number of concurrent client connections allowed by the MySQL server. Increasing this value supports more simultaneous connections but consumes more memory and CPU resources. Primarily used to mitigate connection bottlenecks; it is recommended to set this value reasonably based on system memory and CPU core count, typically between 500 and 2000

max_join_size.desc: The maximum estimated number of rows that can be scanned for a join query without a WHERE condition. This parameter prevents inefficient large join queries from executing, helping to alleviate CPU and memory bottlenecks. Increasing this value allows larger joins to execute but may impact performance

max_length_for_sort_data.desc: The threshold (in bytes) that determines whether to use a more efficient sorting algorithm. When the row data length is less than this value, MySQL uses an improved sorting algorithm to enhance sort performance. Increasing this value improves sorting efficiency, helping to alleviate CPU bottlenecks

max_prepared_stmt_count.desc: The maximum number of prepared statements that can exist simultaneously on the server. Increasing this value supports more prepared statements, reducing SQL parsing overhead and helping to alleviate CPU bottlenecks. New prepared statements return an error when this limit is exceeded

max_sort_length.desc: The maximum number of bytes considered for sorting BLOB or TEXT fields. Only the first N bytes are used for sort comparison. Increasing this value improves sort accuracy but increases memory and CPU overhead, while decreasing it helps alleviate memory bottlenecks

max_user_connections.desc: The maximum number of concurrent connections allowed per user account. A value of 0 indicates no limit. Increasing this value allows a single user to use more connections but may impact overall resource allocation. Primarily used to control resource usage and mitigate memory and CPU contention

min_examined_row_limit.desc: The minimum number of examined rows threshold for slow query log recording. Only queries that examine more rows than this value are eligible to be logged. Increasing this value reduces the amount of slow query logging, helping to filter out queries that scan fewer rows. Primarily affects disk I/O and CPU analysis

back_log.desc: The number of connection requests that can be queued before MySQL temporarily stops accepting new connections. Increasing this value allows handling a large number of connection requests in a short time, helping to alleviate CPU bottlenecks during connection storms. It is recommended to increase this value appropriately in high-concurrency connection scenarios

group_concat_max_len.desc: The maximum length of the result returned by the GROUP_CONCAT() function (in bytes). Increasing this value allows concatenation of longer strings but increases memory usage. Primarily used to mitigate memory bottlenecks and prevent result truncation

join_buffer_size.desc: The buffer size used per session for join operations that cannot use indexes. Increasing this value improves the performance of full table scan joins but increases memory consumption. Primarily used to mitigate disk I/O bottlenecks, suitable for environments with many complex join queries

read_buffer_size.desc: The buffer size used per thread for sequential scans of MyISAM tables. Increasing this value improves sequential read performance but increases memory usage. Primarily used to mitigate disk I/O bottlenecks, suitable for scenarios with many full table scans

read_rnd_buffer_size.desc: The buffer size used for random reads when reading rows in sorted order after sorting. Increasing this value improves ORDER BY operation performance but increases memory overhead. Primarily used to mitigate disk I/O bottlenecks, suitable for scenarios requiring reading large amounts of data after sorting

sort_buffer_size.desc: The buffer size used per session for sort operations. Increasing this value allows more sorting to be done in memory, reducing the use of on-disk temporary files, helping to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks. For complex sorts or large result sets, increasing this value is recommended

table_definition_cache.desc: The number of table definitions (.frm files) that can be cached. Increasing this value reduces the overhead of re-reading table definitions when opening tables, improving concurrent performance and helping to alleviate CPU bottlenecks. It is recommended to increase this value appropriately in environments with many tables

thread_pool_size.desc: The number of thread groups in the thread pool. Increasing this value improves processing capability under high-concurrency connections but may increase context switching overhead. Primarily used to mitigate CPU bottlenecks, suitable for scenarios where the number of connections far exceeds the number of CPU cores

transaction_isolation.desc: The transaction isolation level, which controls visibility and concurrency behavior between transactions. READ-UNCOMMITTED provides the highest concurrency but may allow dirty reads. REPEATABLE-READ is InnoDB's default level, offering a good balance of concurrency and consistency. Choosing the appropriate level can alleviate lock contention and CPU bottlenecks

transaction_read_only.desc: Sets the default read-only mode for transactions. Enabling this mode optimizes the performance of read-only transactions, reduces lock overhead, and helps alleviate CPU and memory bottlenecks. Suitable for application scenarios dominated by read operations

binlog_format.desc: The recording format for the binary log. ROW mode records changes to each row, which is the safest but generates more log data. STATEMENT mode records SQL statements, which generates less log data but may cause inconsistencies. MIXED mode automatically chooses the appropriate format. Choosing the right format balances disk I/O and CPU usage

binlog_group_commit_sync_delay.desc: The delay time (in microseconds) for synchronizing the binary log during group commit. Increasing this value allows more transactions to commit together, reducing the number of disk syncs and helping to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks. Setting a non-zero value can increase throughput but may increase transaction response time

binlog_group_commit_sync_no_delay_count.desc: The minimum number of transactions to trigger group commit synchronization for the binary log. When the number of waiting transactions reaches this value, synchronization is performed immediately, even if the binlog_group_commit_sync_delay time has not elapsed. Increasing this value improves batching efficiency, helping to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks

binlog_row_image.desc: The type of row image recorded in the binary log when using ROW format. 'full' records the complete row, 'minimal' records only changed columns, and 'noblob' records all columns except BLOB types. Choosing the appropriate type reduces log volume, helping to alleviate disk I/O and network bottlenecks

max_binlog_size.desc: The maximum size of a single binary log file (in bytes). When the log file reaches this size, it rotates to a new file. Increasing this value reduces the frequency of file rotation but may increase management overhead for individual files. Primarily used to manage disk I/O and storage space

max_binlog_stmt_cache_size.desc: The maximum size of the binary log statement cache (in bytes). When the statement cache for a transaction exceeds this size, on-disk temporary files are used. Increasing this value reduces the use of on-disk temporary files, helping to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks, suitable for large transaction scenarios

transaction_write_set_extraction.desc: The hash algorithm used to extract transaction write sets. MURMUR32 uses the Murmur32 hash algorithm, while OFF disables extraction. Enabling this feature improves the efficiency of group replication and parallel replication, helping to alleviate CPU bottlenecks. It is recommended to set this to MURMUR32 in group replication environments

innodb_autoextend_increment.desc: The increment size for automatic InnoDB tablespace extension (in MB). Increasing this value reduces the frequency of tablespace extensions, improving batch write performance and helping to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks. The default value of 64 MB is suitable for most scenarios

innodb_autoinc_lock_mode.desc: Controls the lock mechanism used when generating values for auto-increment columns in InnoDB. 0 is the traditional mode using table locks; 1 is consecutive mode using mutex locks; 2 is interleaved mode allowing concurrent inserts. Choosing the appropriate mode can improve concurrent insert performance, helping to alleviate CPU bottlenecks

innodb_buffer_pool_load_abort.desc: Controls whether an ongoing buffer pool load operation is aborted. When set to ON, the load is immediately aborted, used to intervene when the loading process impacts performance. This parameter is primarily used to manage the buffer pool warm-up process and alleviate disk I/O pressure during startup

innodb_deadlock_detect.desc: Enables or disables InnoDB's deadlock detection mechanism. When enabled, the system automatically detects and rolls back deadlocked transactions. When disabled, it relies on innodb_lock_wait_timeout to avoid infinite waiting. Disabling deadlock detection reduces CPU overhead under high concurrency, helping to alleviate CPU bottlenecks

innodb_fill_factor.desc: The fill factor percentage for each B-tree page when InnoDB creates or rebuilds indexes. A smaller value reserves more space within pages, reducing subsequent splits but consuming more disk space. Increasing this value improves space utilization, helping to alleviate disk I/O and memory bottlenecks

innodb_flush_log_at_timeout.desc: The timeout period for InnoDB log flushing (in seconds). Even when innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit is set to 0 or 2, logs are flushed periodically at this interval. Increasing this value reduces the frequency of flushes, helping to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks, but may increase the risk of data loss during crash recovery

innodb_flush_neighbors.desc: Controls whether adjacent pages are also flushed when InnoDB flushes dirty pages. 0 means do not flush neighbors, 1 means flush neighbors, and 2 means flush neighbors within the same extent. For SSD devices, setting this to 0 is recommended to reduce unnecessary writes, helping to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks

innodb_flush_sync.desc: Controls whether InnoDB performs synchronous flushing during checkpoints. When enabled (ON), it enforces synchronous I/O during checkpoint periods, improving data safety but potentially impacting performance. Primarily used to balance data durability and disk I/O bottlenecks

innodb_lru_scan_depth.desc: The scan depth of the InnoDB LRU list, which determines the number of pages scanned each time by the page cleaner threads. Increasing this value improves the efficiency of dirty page flushing but increases CPU usage. Primarily used to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks; it is recommended to adjust this value based on write load

innodb_max_purge_lag_delay.desc: The maximum delay (in microseconds) imposed on INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations when purge lag occurs. Increasing this value limits DML delays caused by purge lag, helping to alleviate memory bottlenecks but may reduce overall throughput

innodb_max_undo_log_size.desc: The maximum size of the InnoDB undo log file (in bytes). When the undo log exceeds this value, a truncation operation is triggered. Increasing this value reduces the frequency of undo log truncation, helping to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks but increases disk space usage

innodb_numa_interleave.desc: Controls whether InnoDB uses a NUMA-interleaved memory allocation policy. When enabled, memory is balanced across multiple NUMA nodes, improving memory access performance on multi-core systems. Primarily used to mitigate memory bottlenecks and enhance performance on large-memory servers

innodb_online_alter_log_max_size.desc: The maximum size (in bytes) of the temporary log used to record concurrent DML operations during online DDL operations. Increasing this value supports larger online DDL operations, helping to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks and avoid DDL operation failures

innodb_purge_batch_size.desc: The number of undo log records processed per batch in purge operations. Increasing this value improves the efficiency of purge operations but increases CPU usage per purge. Primarily used to mitigate memory bottlenecks, suitable for high write load environments

innodb_random_read_ahead.desc: Controls whether InnoDB enables random read-ahead. When enabled, pages are pre-read into the buffer pool based on page access patterns, improving random read performance. Primarily used to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks, suitable for scenarios with frequent random read patterns

innodb_sort_buffer_size.desc: The size of the sort buffer used by InnoDB during index creation or rebuild (in bytes). Increasing this value allows more sorting to be done in memory, reducing the use of on-disk temporary files, helping to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks

innodb_stats_auto_recalc.desc: Controls whether InnoDB automatically recalculates persistent statistics when table data changes by more than 10%. Enabling this helps the optimizer make better execution plans but increases CPU overhead. Primarily used to alleviate query performance bottlenecks; it is recommended to keep this enabled

innodb_stats_persistent.desc: Controls whether InnoDB statistics are persisted to disk. When enabled, statistics are retained after restart, avoiding recomputation each time the server starts, helping to alleviate CPU bottlenecks during startup. It is recommended to keep this enabled

innodb_stats_persistent_sample_pages.desc: The number of index pages sampled when collecting persistent statistics. Increasing this value improves the accuracy of statistics, helping the optimizer make better execution plans, but increases CPU and disk I/O overhead during statistics calculation

innodb_undo_log_truncate.desc: Controls whether InnoDB automatically truncates undo log files that exceed the maximum size. Enabling this reclaims disk space, helping to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks. It is recommended to enable this parameter when innodb_max_undo_log_size is also enabled

innodb_dedicated_server.desc: Automatically configures InnoDB parameters to suit server resources when MySQL is running on a dedicated server. When enabled, key parameters such as innodb_buffer_pool_size are automatically set, helping to optimize CPU and memory usage. It is recommended to enable this in dedicated server environments

innodb_doublewrite_batch_size.desc: The number of pages written per batch in the doublewrite buffer. Increasing this value improves the batching efficiency of doublewrite operations, helping to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks. When set to 0, the default value is used; it is recommended to adjust this based on write load

innodb_doublewrite_files.desc: The number of doublewrite files. Increasing the number of files improves the concurrency of doublewrite operations, helping to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks, especially in scenarios using multiple disk devices. The default value of 2 is suitable for most configurations

innodb_doublewrite_pages.desc: The number of pages written per doublewrite batch. Increasing this value improves the throughput of doublewrite operations, helping to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks but increases memory usage. It is recommended to adjust this in conjunction with innodb_doublewrite_batch_size

innodb_fsync_threshold.desc: The threshold for fsync operations (in bytes), used to control the frequency of file synchronization at the operating system level. Increasing this value reduces the number of fsync calls, improving write performance and helping to alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks, but may increase the risk of data loss

binlog_expire_logs_seconds.desc: The number of seconds after which binary log files automatically expire. Binary logs older than this value are automatically deleted to manage disk space. Increasing this value retains logs for a longer period for recovery and replication, but increases disk I/O and storage pressure

binlog_transaction_compression.desc: Enables binary log transaction compression. When enabled, it significantly reduces the disk usage and network transfer size of the binary log, helping to alleviate disk I/O and network bottlenecks, but increases CPU usage (compression and decompression overhead)

binlog_transaction_compression_level_zst.desc: The compression level for binary logs when using the Zstd algorithm, ranging from 1 to 22. Higher levels provide better compression ratios but consume more CPU. Increasing this value further reduces log size but increases CPU load. Primarily used to balance disk I/O and CPU bottlenecks
